title: TCP Congestion Control: How cwnd Moves

slides.title: Two limits on sending
slides.description: A sender keeps at most min(cwnd, rwnd) bytes unacknowledged. The receiver sets rwnd; the sender guesses cwnd from loss.

slides.title: Slow start
slides.description: Every ACK adds 1 MSS to cwnd, so cwnd doubles each round trip until it reaches ssthresh or a loss is detected.

slides.title: Congestion avoidance
slides.description: Above ssthresh, growth becomes additive: about 1 MSS per round trip, probing slowly for spare capacity.
slides.code: per ACK: cwnd += MSS × MSS / cwnd

slides.title: 3 duplicate ACKs
slides.description: Duplicate ACKs mean one segment is missing but later ones arrived, so the path still works. Reno retransmits at once.
rows: back to slide 3, no slow start

slides.title: Timeout: the hard reset
slides.description: A retransmission timeout means ACKs stopped arriving. The sender assumes heavy congestion and restarts small.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.description: Start with cwnd 1 MSS and ssthresh 16. At cwnd 20, three duplicate ACKs arrive; no timeout happens.
